```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5
)

theme_measure_sec <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white")
    )
}
```

## Scope

This vignette shows summary and slice tables, a comparison result, and a local
CSV export. The summary examples use the package's supplied polystyrene
standard table. The chromatogram example uses a synthetic `sec_triple_detect`
trace. These examples demonstrate the export functions; they do not validate a
calibration or a method.

The CSV files created during rendering are written to `tempdir()`. Report,
Excel, database, and Arrow examples later in the vignette remain unevaluated;
they are templates that require local paths or optional software.

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(measure)
library(measure.sec)
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

## Summary table

`measure_sec_summary_table()` collects molecular-weight averages and any
additional columns requested. Here it formats the values supplied with
`sec_ps_standards` and carries the modal mass (`mp`) as an additional column.

```{r summary-table}
data(sec_ps_standards, package = "measure.sec")

summary_input <- sec_ps_standards |>
  transmute(
    sample_id = standard_name,
    mp_da = mp,
    mw_mn = mn,
    mw_mw = mw,
    mw_dispersity = dispersity
  )

summary_tbl <- measure_sec_summary_table(
  summary_input,
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  additional_cols = "mp_da",
  digits = 2
)

print(summary_tbl)
```

The figure uses the averages in the supplied standard table. It is a view of
the package data, not an analysis of a newly measured chromatogram.

```{r summary-view, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Molecular-weight averages from the supplied standard table, returned by `measure_sec_summary_table()` and plotted against each standard's supplied modal mass.", fig.alt = "Log-log scatter chart of supplied modal mass in Da versus number-average and weight-average molecular weight in Da for 16 polystyrene standards. Two colored point series rise with modal mass; number-average values are below weight-average values."}
summary_plot_data <- summary_tbl |>
  as_tibble() |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mw_mn, mw_mw),
    names_to = "average",
    values_to = "molecular_weight"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    average = recode(
      average,
      mw_mn = "Number average (Mn)",
      mw_mw = "Weight average (Mw)"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  summary_plot_data,
  aes(x = mp_da, y = molecular_weight, colour = average, group = average)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Number average (Mn)" = "#2E86AB",
      "Weight average (Mw)" = "#A23B72"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Supplied modal mass (Da)",
    y = "Supplied molecular-weight average (Da)",
    colour = "Average"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

## Comparing standards

`measure_sec_compare()` returns a summary and differences from a selected
reference. This example compares three rows from the same supplied standard
table; it does not represent batch release results.

```{r compare-standards}
comparison_rows <- summary_tbl |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(sample_id %in% c("PS-430000", "PS-216000", "PS-120000"))

comparison <- measure_sec_compare(
  comparison_rows |> filter(sample_id == "PS-430000"),
  comparison_rows |> filter(sample_id == "PS-216000"),
  comparison_rows |> filter(sample_id == "PS-120000"),
  samples = c("PS-430000", "PS-216000", "PS-120000"),
  metrics = "mw_averages",
  plot = FALSE,
  reference = "PS-430000"
)

comparison$summary
comparison$differences
```

```{r comparison-view, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Percent differences in supplied weight-average molecular weight from the PS-430000 reference, using the `differences` table returned by `measure_sec_compare()`.", fig.alt = "Horizontal dot chart of percent difference in weight-average molecular weight relative to PS-430000. The PS-216000 and PS-120000 reference rows fall below zero because their supplied weight-average values are lower than the selected reference."}
comparison_plot_data <- comparison$differences |>
  filter(sample != "PS-430000")

ggplot(
  comparison_plot_data,
  aes(x = mw_mw_pct, y = sample)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey45", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = "#A23B72", size = 2.4) +
  labs(
    x = "Difference in Mw from PS-430000 (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

## Slice table from a chromatogram

Long format is convenient for plotting and interchange. This example converts
a single synthetic PS-100K chromatogram to the measure format, corrects its RI
baseline, and extracts slice values.

```{r process-for-slices}
data(sec_triple_detect, package = "measure.sec")

ps_sample <- sec_triple_detect |>
  filter(sample_id == "PS-100K")

rec <- recipe(
  ri_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = ps_sample
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri")

chromatogram_data <- prep(rec) |>
  bake(new_data = NULL)

slices_long <- measure_sec_slice_table(
  chromatogram_data,
  measures = "ri",
  sample_id = "sample_id"
)

head(slices_long, 10)
```

```{r slice-view, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "The baseline-corrected RI slice table for the synthetic PS-100K example, plotted against its stored elution-time locations.", fig.alt = "Line chart of elution time in minutes versus baseline-corrected RI detector response in its native units for the synthetic PS-100K trace. The signal forms one broad peak in the middle of the displayed elution range and approaches baseline on either side."}
ggplot(slices_long, aes(x = location, y = value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2E86AB", linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "Baseline-corrected RI signal (native units)"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

## Wide slice tables

Wide format gives each measure its own column. It can be useful when exporting
several aligned measures from the same baked recipe.

```{r slice-wide}
slices_wide <- measure_sec_slice_table(
  chromatogram_data,
  measures = "ri",
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  pivot = TRUE
)

head(slices_wide)
```

## Write CSV files to a temporary directory

These two files are written to the current R session's temporary directory.
They are not saved in the package or vignette source tree.

```{r csv-export}
export_dir <- tempdir()
summary_csv <- file.path(export_dir, "sec_summary_table.csv")
slices_csv <- file.path(export_dir, "sec_slice_data.csv")

utils::write.csv(as.data.frame(summary_tbl), summary_csv, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(slices_long, slices_csv, row.names = FALSE)

tibble::tibble(
  file = basename(c(summary_csv, slices_csv)),
  bytes = file.info(c(summary_csv, slices_csv))$size
)
```

## Other export targets

The following chunks are not run when this vignette is rendered. They show
optional local integrations; set paths and connection details for your own
environment before running them.

### Excel workbook

```{r excel-export, eval=FALSE}
# Requires the optional writexl package.
excel_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_results.xlsx")

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    Summary = as.data.frame(summary_tbl),
    `Slice Data` = slices_long
  ),
  excel_file
)
```

### Database

```{r db-export, eval=FALSE}
# Requires DBI and RSQLite. The example database path is temporary.
db_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_results.sqlite")
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = db_file)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "sec_results", as.data.frame(summary_tbl), append = TRUE)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

### GraphPad Prism

```{r prism-export, eval=FALSE}
prism_data <- slices_long |>
  select(location, sample_id, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = value)

prism_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_for_prism.csv")
utils::write.csv(prism_data, prism_file, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Python-readable files

```{r python-export, eval=FALSE}
# Requires the optional arrow package.
feather_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_data.feather")
parquet_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_data.parquet")

arrow::write_feather(slices_long, feather_file)
arrow::write_parquet(slices_long, parquet_file)
```

## Reports

Report generation can write files and may require Quarto or other local
software. These examples remain unevaluated during rendering; each output path
points to `tempdir()`.

```{r standard-report, eval=FALSE}
measure_sec_report(
  as.data.frame(summary_tbl),
  template = "standard",
  output_format = "html",
  output_file = file.path(tempdir(), "sec_standard_report.html"),
  title = "SEC analysis summary",
  open = FALSE
)
```

```{r detailed-report, eval=FALSE}
measure_sec_report(
  as.data.frame(summary_tbl),
  template = "detailed",
  output_format = "pdf",
  output_file = file.path(tempdir(), "sec_detailed_report.pdf"),
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  include_slice_table = TRUE
)
```

A QC report needs peak-level input and criteria from the method. Those objects
are not part of the standard-table example.

```{r qc-report, eval=FALSE}
measure_sec_report(
  integration_peak_table,
  template = "qc",
  output_format = "html",
  output_file = file.path(tempdir(), "sec_qc_report.html"),
  specs = method_criteria
)
```

## Traceability fields

Attach provenance fields from the actual run record. The placeholders below
are intentionally empty because no analyst or instrument record is included
with the supplied standard table.

```{r traceability, eval=FALSE}
summary_with_audit <- as.data.frame(summary_tbl) |>
  mutate(
    analysis_date = as.Date(NA),
    analyst = NA_character_,
    instrument = NA_character_,
    column = NA_character_,
    measure_sec_version = as.character(packageVersion("measure.sec"))
  )
```

For reproducibility, store the calibration object and analysis settings used
for the actual sample. The path below is temporary; replace the placeholder
calibration name with the object or identifier from your run.

```{r save-parameters, eval=FALSE}
analysis_params <- list(
  date = Sys.time(),
  calibration = calibration_object,
  baseline_method = "linear",
  package_version = packageVersion("measure.sec")
)

parameter_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "sec_analysis_parameters.rds")
saveRDS(analysis_params, parameter_file)
```

## Troubleshooting

### Missing molecular-weight columns

Check that the input to `measure_sec_summary_table()` contains `Mn`, `Mw`,
`Mz`, or their `mw_`-prefixed names.

```{r troubleshoot-missing, eval=FALSE}
names(processed_results)
```

### Empty slice table

Confirm that the baked recipe contains measure columns before calling
`measure_sec_slice_table()`.

```{r troubleshoot-empty, eval=FALSE}
measure::find_measure_cols(processed_results)
```
